description: Record `<lockFile>.predecessor.json` next to a lock file: the process domain the last holder created while it held the lock. The next holder must find that domain empty before it may proceed.

file.writer: the holder, right after acquire and BEFORE it creates the domain, while it still holds the lock (nobody reads it mid-write)
file.writeMode: write a temp file next to it, then rename over the record
file.absentMeaning: the previous holder created no domain: nothing to wait for

linux-gate.meaning: process tuple of the gate; the domain is empty iff judge(tuple) == dead

linux-pgroup.meaning: process tuple of the group leader (Linux without user namespaces, best-effort); the domain is empty when judge(tuple) == dead and no process is left in its process group

windows-job.sessionId: string, the Windows session of the holder

holder.startTime: string, creation FILETIME as a decimal string

windows-job.keeper: { host, pid, startTime } | null; filled by rewriting the record (temp + rename) right after the keeper's ack and before any member exists
windows-job.meaning: named kill-on-close Job Object plus the process tuples that bound the tree view. A string domainId (the old shape) is an unknown shape and stays fail-closed.

macos-tree.meaning: tuple of the tree root; the domain is empty when no process is left in its process group nor in the scanned descendant tree (best-effort)

record.unknownVersion: a record with v != 1 or an unreadable record is never deleted or ignored: acquire returns held (predecessor-domain-not-empty) with the raw record

releaseRule.text: A holder releases only when its own domain is empty: wait for the child, kill what is left in the domain, wait for empty, then release. A non-empty predecessor domain after the next holder took the lock therefore means the previous holder died abnormally.

acquireAlgorithm: read the predecessor record; absent -> proceed
ask the driver whether the domain is empty; empty or unopenable-but-proven-empty -> proceed
not empty -> kill the whole domain at once (never wait for it to drain)
wait up to killWaitMs for the killed processes to be signaled
domain empty -> proceed; deadline passed -> release the kernel lock and return held (predecessor-domain-not-empty) naming the domain
after proceeding, a holder that will create a domain itself overwrites the record before creating it

jobView.usedBy: the release rule (step 0) and the keeper
jobView.empty: ActiveProcesses == 0 AND every member ever named by the job's process id list, plus every process Toolhelp reports as IsProcessInJob, is signaled
jobView.never: uses the holder tree, includes the holder or the keeper, kills outside the job, or opens a snapshot in the keeper

contenderView.usedBy: admit, after the kernel lock is held; re-read on every poll
contenderView.holderAlive: recorded holder (pid + creation time) alive: it released normally. Judge with the job view; if not empty, TerminateJobObject only. Never signal the holder or the keeper.
contenderView.holderDead: union of three sources: (1) the job list; (2) the in-job scan; (3) the tree = descendants of the recorded holder created at or after declaredAt, excluding the keeper tuple. Empty only when all three are empty.
contenderView.failClosed: a tree process whose parent is a tree node but whose creation time cannot be read, and any named pid whose OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE) fails with anything but ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, is an unopenable member: while present in the snapshot the domain is not empty
contenderView.jobNotOpenable: Toolhelp fallback over the tree source only, same rules, and two consecutive quiet snapshots are required
contenderView.kill: TerminateJobObject, plus a kill by identity for tree members that are not in the job
contenderView.otherSession: record sessionId differs from the contender's session: not empty, reason predecessor-other-session; the fallback is never used across sessions

windowsJobViews.keeperExit: the job-keeper exits only when BOTH hold: (i) the holder wrote its finished line, or the holder's handle is signaled; and (ii) the job view is empty. It polls every 50 ms with the list and count only, and never exits because its stdin closed.
windowsJobViews.unknownShape: v stays 1; a windows-job record whose domainId is not this object is unknown and judged not empty

killWaitMs.meaning: only bounds the wait for processes that were already terminated to be signaled

driverSupport.linux-gate: implemented: judge(gate) == dead; kill_all = SIGKILL by identity
driverSupport.linux-pgroup: written by the run supervisor (containment.port.v1.json); until its driver lands a holder-lock driver answers unknown, which is never treated as empty
driverSupport.windows-job: implemented by the Windows driver: contender view and job view above
driverSupport.macos-tree: contract only until a consumer declares a tree domain; best-effort

runBorrowedWithoutDomain: On Linux run_borrowed declares no domain; the leftovers it kills are the other processes that still hold the lock description (holders()). On macOS the leftovers are the child's process group.
